leh-manali-highway-lachulung-la-leh.provenance: CURATED FROM THE ARCHIVE: waypoints taken from the named road Leh–Manali Highway. Distances between stops are great-circle with a road factor, not a routed measurement - the pipeline replaces them when it routes this line.

scenicChapters.title: Leh–Manali Highway
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 5328 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Tanglang La → Leh
scenicChapters.narrative: 271 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it. This is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.

leh-manali-highway-lachulung-la-leh.story: The highest point is about 5,350 m. Lachulung La and Tanglang La are open in summer only - check it is open before you set off. It suits an unhurried touring pace.

scenicChapters.narrative: Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast. For 85 km this is North Macedonia Mavrovo and Galicnik Route, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it.

facts.v: North Macedonia Mavrovo and Galicnik Route

places-rrajca-church-of-the-virgin-of-le.story: 305 km from Labunista to Labunista, about 5 h 16 of riding. It goes by way of Dlaboka Reka, Church of the Virgin of Leviša and back through Dlaboka Reka. The highest point is about 1,500 m. It crosses Albania, North Macedonia and Kosovo - carry ID and check vignette or toll rules. It was put together for the scenery rather than the shortest line.
